scenes.heading: Interactions that drive evolution
scenes.say: No species evolves alone. What it eats, competes with, is eaten by, or depends on are some of the strongest forces of natural selection it faces.

scenes.heading: Score it with +, − and 0
scenes.say: Score each interaction by its effect on both partners. Competition is minus, minus. Predation, herbivory and parasitism are plus, minus. Mutualism is plus, plus, like clownfish and anemones. Commensalism is plus, zero.
scenes.caption: Score each interaction by its effect on both partners. Competition is − / −. Predation, herbivory and parasitism are + / −. Mutualism is + / +, like clownfish and anemones. Commensalism is + / 0.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Two food trucks selling the same burgers: one goes out of business
scenes.science: Two species can't share exactly the same limiting resource forever
scenes.breaks: Species don't decide to change their 'menu': differences grow over generations because individuals that compete less leave more offspring.
scenes.say: Two food trucks selling identical burgers at the footy: the slightly cheaper one takes all the customers. That's competitive exclusion. They can survive side by side by splitting the market, which is resource partitioning. Over time, their menus can grow more different: character displacement.

scenes.heading: A removal experiment
scenes.question: Barnacle P lives only high on the rocks. When species Q is removed, what happens to P?
scenes.say: Barnacle P lives only high on the rocks. Remove species Q, and P's cover in the middle zone jumps from two to forty-five percent. So P could live lower, but Q excludes it. P's realised niche is smaller than its fundamental niche.
scenes.caption: Barnacle P lives only high on the rocks. Remove species Q, and P's cover in the middle zone jumps from 2% to 45%. So P could live lower, but Q excludes it. P's realised niche is smaller than its fundamental niche.

scenes.heading: Two kinds of mimicry

left.title: Batesian = Bluffing
points: Fails if mimics get too common

scenes.say: Batesian is bluffing: a harmless hoverfly looks like a stinging wasp. It only works while real wasps are common. Müllerian is mutual warning: several harmful species share one pattern, so predators learn to avoid them all faster.

scenes.heading: Coevolution
points: A rally, not a one-way serve
Arms race: toxic newts, resistant snakes
Red Queen: run to stay in place
scenes.say: Coevolution needs a rally, not a one-way serve: both species must change in response to each other. Toxic newts and resistant garter snakes escalate together in an arms race. And the Red Queen idea says species keep evolving just to keep up.

scenes.heading: Mutualism isn't friendship
points: Each is selected to gain at lowest cost
Legumes cut oxygen to lazy nodules
scenes.say: Mutualism is like a group assignment: everyone does better together, but each member is tempted to slack off. Cheaters steal nectar without pollinating. Legumes punish slackers by cutting oxygen to root nodules that fix little nitrogen.

Quick recap. Score interactions with plus, minus and zero. Competition drives resource partitioning and character displacement. Batesian mimics bluff. Coevolution is two-way. And remember, selection has no foresight. Now try the practice questions!
